title: In, then out
summary: A real spike is sodium rushing in, then potassium pushing back.

cards.text:
Sodium rushes in.
That pushes the voltage higher, which lets more sodium in.

Then the sodium door closes,
and potassium pushes the voltage back down.

The simple brim is a stand-in for that fight.
Use the ions when the shape of the fight is the question.

question.prompt: What carries the upward rush of a real spike?
question.why: Sodium entry is the upstroke. Potassium restores.
question.simpler: Inward sodium first. Outward potassium after.

recall.question: Which ion rushes in to make the upstroke?

deeper.note: Hodgkin and Huxley separated the currents with a voltage clamp. Read the logic in the introduction. Skip the rate tables on the train.
